name: Muzo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Colombian isolate; only colonial wordlists (Castillo Mathieu 1972; Durbin & Seijas 1973); no phonology exists.

sources.citation: del Castillo Mathieu, Nicolas. 1972. El vocabulario muzo-colima de la Relacion de Juan Suarez de Cepeda (1582). Thesaurus (Boletin del Instituto Caro y Cuervo) 27(3): 413-441.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 5 'Lexico muzo-colima' (pp. 424-428) reprints c. 100 words from Suarez de Cepeda's Relaciones of 1581/1582 and Simon in the 16th-c. orthography (c->z, q->c only), then Carib etymologies; no accent marks on entries, no remark on accent, stress, syllables or prosody anywhere (grep acent/tonic/prosod/silab: none).

sources.citation: Loukotka, Cestmir. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center. (Muzo entry, Pijao group)
sources.note: Nothing; entry reads 'Muzo - once spoken at the sources of the Carare River and in the Paima Valley, department of Cundinamarca. [Simon 1882-1892, vol. 3, pp. 103-223 passim, only five words; Urdaneta 1924, pp. 472-476 passim, only three words.]'

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul. 1943. La influencia karib en Colombia. Revista del Instituto Etnologico Nacional 1(1): 55-93. Bogota.
sources.note: Nothing on Muzo. pp. 68-69: Colima-Muzo toponyms in -pi/-pa and the c. 15 words saved by Simon, marked (M)/(C), no accent marks; the only 'acento' remark (p. 71 n.) is about Antioquia river names in -na having final rather than penultimate stress, not Muzo.

sources.citation: Simon, Fray Pedro. 1882-1892 [1627]. Noticias historiales de las conquistas de Tierra Firme en las Indias occidentales, vol. III. Bogota: Medardo Rivas. (archive.org scanned text tierrafirmeindias03simbrich)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p. 220 (Noticia 7, cap. XXIII, par. 3) is the only extant remark on Muzo-Colima pronunciation: 'La lengua de todos es una y general, llana y de buena pronunciacion, por no tener nada de gutural, y asi se puede muy bien escribir; en toda ella no se pronuncia la L.' -- 'llana' here means plain/smooth (paired with 'nada de gutural'), not paroxytone. The 'Marquita, el acento en la i' remark (scanned line 5400) concerns the Spanish town name Mariquita in Panche country.
Nothing; Unclassifiable, extinct (AES 10), no references listed at all (consistent with n_glottolog_desc_refs = 0).
